03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

A Claude skill for anything written against the Fusion Python API (adsk.core, adsk.fusion). It starts every add-in from tested templates that already obey four rules which, when broken, cause most "my add-in does nothing" reports: keep handler references alive, tear everything down in stop(), mind the document type, and wrap every entry point in try/except.

It covers two kinds of tool. Productivity and UI tools drive what's already there: buttons and dropdowns, built-in commands, selection, visibility, the browser tree, renaming, the timeline and the camera. Geometry tools create sketches, bodies, features and parameters. Six reference files hold the templates, the UI recipes, dialog inputs, error handling, document types and geometry recipes; installers come from the fusion-addin-installer skill.

It is the foundation layer: fusion-palette-addin builds Swami's house-spec palette tools on top of its rules.

Why it mattersFusion's API fails quietly. A garbage-collected handler, a missing teardown or a component call in the wrong document type gives no error, just a button that does nothing. Starting from templates that already avoid these saves the debugging.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • Script or Add-inDecides whether you need a run-once script or a resident add-in with run(), stop() and a manifest; when in doubt it builds an add-in.
  • TemplatesStarts from one of six templates in references/templates.md: manifest, command-button (the default), simple-script, palette (HTML UI), event-only, and a command factory that builds many similar commands from one table. The palette template builds its page path from the add-in's own folder, so it loads the same way everywhere.
  • UI ToolsUses references/ui-navigation.md to fire built-in commands (and find their IDs), read and set the selection, walk entities, show, hide or isolate them, place buttons in panels or dropdowns, rename in the browser, work the timeline, and move the camera.
  • GeometryUses references/geometry-recipes.md for sketches, extrudes, user parameters, fillets, patterns and booleans.
  • DialogsUses references/command-inputs.md for message boxes and command dialogs: text, value, dropdown, checkbox, radio, slider, selection, groups, tabs and tables, live updates and validation.
  • Error HandlingUses references/error-handling.md: expected versus unexpected errors, guard clauses, rolling back a half-finished change, collecting batch errors, and treating Cancel as a normal exit.
  • Document TypesUses references/document-types.md to guard component creation: Part-type documents have no occurrence tree, so it works on the root component there.
  • Icons and ShortcutsAdds 16, 32 and 64 px icons (or one SVG), checks several icons side by side so no two match, and tells you how to bind a keyboard shortcut.
  • InstallersAdds the double-click installers and README.txt, built with the fusion-addin-installer skill, unless you only want source code to read.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Two Kinds of ToolHandles both UI and productivity tools and geometry tools, and tools that mix them.
  • Rich DialogsBuilds native command dialogs with every input type, live updates and validation, or a message box when that's enough.
  • Many CommandsThe command factory builds a whole family of similar commands (show, hide, isolate per entity type) from one table.
  • Safe BatchesBatch work reports which items failed instead of stopping at the first, and a failed multi-step change can be rolled back.
  • DebuggingDiagnoses add-ins that won't load, buttons that do nothing, duplicate buttons, and component creation failing in Part documents.
  • Can't Run FusionClaude can compile and inspect the code but can't run it in Fusion; you test it live.
  • Undocumented IDsBuilt-in command IDs and panel IDs aren't fully documented and change between versions. The skill shows how to discover them rather than guessing, and flags uncertain API names.
  • Modal CommandsSome built-in commands open their own dialog when executed and can't run headless; the operation then has to be rebuilt with the API.
  • No Themed DialogsNative command dialogs can't be themed; only HTML palettes can take the dark style.
  • Out of ScopeNot for Fusion dashboards or HTML deliverables, CAM post-processors, or other CAD programs.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Garbage-collected HandlersA handler not kept in the module-level handlers list is silently collected: the button appears but clicking does nothing.
  • Missing TeardownEvery control, command definition and palette added in run() must be deleted in stop(), or reloading causes "identity already exists" errors or duplicate buttons. Dropdowns need deeper teardown.
  • Part DocumentsaddNewComponent() fails in a Part-type document, which has no occurrence tree. Check the document type, or work on rootComponent directly.
  • Silent FailuresFusion swallows unhandled exceptions. Every entry point needs try/except with traceback.format_exc() in a message box.
  • CentimetersA value input's .value is always in centimeters (radians for angles), whatever the document units: "50 mm" reads as 5.0. Treating it as millimeters makes geometry ten times too big.
  • Names Must MatchThe folder, .py and .manifest must share one name or Fusion won't list the add-in.
  • No Icon, No ShortcutFusion only offers Change Keyboard Shortcut on a command with an icon folder and a reachable button.
  • Repeated IconsEach icon can look fine alone but match another in the toolbar; render them side by side at 16 px.
  • Direct ModelingSome features fail in a direct-modeling (no history) document; check designType.
  • Message Boxes in LoopsDon't call ui.messageBox inside a loop; log with app.log and show one summary at the end.
  • Windows: Extract FirstRun the installer from an extracted folder, not from inside the zip; SmartScreen may need More info › Run anyway. The README.txt covers both.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • FusionAutodesk Fusion installed and run at least once for the current user, on macOS or on Windows 10 or 11.
  • Code ExecutionOptional but useful: code execution ("Create and edit files") lets Claude compile the code, draw icons and zip the folder.
  • No Admin RightsAdd-ins install into per-user folders; no administrator password is needed.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
Add-inFusion APIA resident Python program with run() and stop() that Fusion loads and keeps running; it can add buttons and react to events.
ScriptFusion APIA Python program that runs once, top to bottom, then exits.
ManifestFusion APIThe JSON file Fusion reads to list an add-in: id, version, product, platforms and run-on-startup.
Event handlerFusion APIAn object Fusion calls when something happens; it must stay referenced or it is garbage-collected.
TeardownFusion APIDeleting every control, command definition and palette in stop().
Command definitionFusion APIFusion's record of a command, which buttons point to; built-in commands have one too.
Command IDFusion APIThe string that names a command, such as FusionFilletCommand; not fully documented, so the skill shows how to discover them.
PaletteFusion UIAn HTML panel inside Fusion, used when a native dialog isn't rich enough.
Command dialogFusion UIFusion's native input window, built from command inputs in commandCreated.
DropdownFusion UIA menu that groups several related commands under one button in a panel.
Keyboard shortcutFusion UIA hotkey the user binds in Fusion; only offered for commands with an icon and a button.
Root componentDocumentsThe top component of a design; safe to add geometry to in any document type.
OccurrenceDocumentsA placed instance of a component in an assembly; Part-type documents have none.
Part documentDocumentsA flat, single-component document type in which new components can't be added.
Direct modelingDocumentsA design with no timeline history; some features behave differently or aren't available.
Internal unitsDocumentsThe units the API always uses: centimeters for length and radians for angles.
Guard clauseErrorsA check at the start of a command that stops with a clear message when a precondition isn't met.
TracebackErrorsPython's error report showing where it failed; shown in a message box so failures aren't silent.
Command factoryTemplatesThe template that builds many similar commands from one table with one shared handler.
